ui_bugs.issue: `_recently_read_at` stamp is lost on drawer re-open. handleOpenChange→fetchItems replaces items wholesale; the amber recently-read pulse therefore never shows on a re-open within the 5-min window. Spec NOTIF-3 explicitly requires persistence across re-open.
ui_bugs.fix_suggestion: In fetchItems, merge incoming server items with previous items' `_recently_read_at` stamps. e.g. `setItems(prev => (r.items||[]).map(n => { const old = prev.find(p => p.id === n.id); return old?._recently_read_at ? { ...n, _recently_read_at: old._recently_read_at } : n; }))`. Or persist stamp in localStorage keyed by notification id with TTL = RECENT_READ_MS.

critical_code_review_comments: NotificationBell.jsx (423 lines) — fetchItems wholesale-replaces items, losing all transient client-only state including `_recently_read_at`. Should merge with previous on every refresh.

_recently_read_at lives only in React component memory. Survives in-tab navigation only if the bell isn't unmounted; a hard reload or tab close loses it. If the spec wants 5-min persistence, store {notif_id → timestamp} in localStorage with TTL filter.

rca_of_the_issue: NOTIF-3 root cause — NotificationBell.handleOpenChange calls fetchItems on every open, which calls setItems(r.items || []) and discards the `_recently_read_at` field set transiently in onItemClick. The spec asks for the amber 'recently-read' pulse to be visible for 5 minutes after a click, which implies it must survive at least one drawer close+open cycle. Fix: merge prior items' `_recently_read_at` into the freshly fetched list (or persist {id: ts} in localStorage with TTL=RECENT_READ_MS=300000).
